references.text: Aaron and his sons were commanded not to leave the entrance of the tabernacle during their consecration, because the Lord's anointing oil was upon them.
Moses poured the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him to sanctify him, illustrating the significance of the anointing oil mentioned in Leviticus 21:12.
The instruction to pour anointing oil over the high priest at his consecration establishes that he is set apart for God.
The description of the holy anointing oil used to consecrate priests and the sanctuary.
The Nazirite was also not to make himself unclean even for his father or mother, similar restrictions that apply to the high priest.
Ezekiel's laws concerning priests and their restrictions regarding uncleanness, reflecting the rules in Leviticus 21.
Jesus as the perfect high priest who is holy, innocent, pure, set apart from sinners and exalted above the heavens.
